title: Hello World
summary: Every programming journey starts with printing your first message. A "Hello World" program proves your tools work and shows the basic shape
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Every programming journey starts with printing your first message. A "Hello World" program proves your tools work and shows the basic shape of a program: code goes in, output comes out.
Read the example line by line. The only job of this program is to send the text "Hello, World!" to the screen. Once you can do this, every other program is just bigger versions of the same idea.
Key points: programs run top to bottom, output functions differ per language, and small programs build confidence.

sections.codeExample:
section .data
    msg db "Hello, World!", 10
section .text
    global _start
_start:
    mov eax, 4
    mov ebx, 1
    mov ecx, msg
    mov edx, 14
    int 0x80
    mov eax, 1
    xor ebx, ebx
    int 0x80
